measured_findings: The upgrade path runs through a real OpenZeppelin TimelockController -- the three role constants are present -- whose getMinDelay() is zero. The delay a timelock exists to impose is not configured, so a queued upgrade can execute in the same block.
The bridge exposes no pause and no per-message admission parameter; the access-control surface is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MAPPER_ROLE.
Verification is by checkpoint: the RootChainManager reads a checkpoint manager fed by the validator set, and exits are proven against it.
PROPOSER_ROLE and EXECUTOR_ROLE are both held by Safe 0xFa7D2a99… (5-of-9). TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE is the Timelock itself (standard OZ). CheckpointManager.owner() is the same Timelock.
getMinDelay()=0 is current live configuration (read 2026-08-24), not merely an unset storage slot — a queued upgrade can execute in the same block.
verdict_reasoning: No configurable parameter gates inbound value per message, so there is nowhere to install a graduated bound. The zero-delay timelock is a separate observation about the upgrade path rather than the reason for the verdict.
caveat: Validator/Safe party-level overlap not address-tested (Heimdall set not on L1 as EOAs).
